definitions.meaning: The force between two surfaces in contact that opposes their relative slide - which is why it can point forward on a driving wheel.
The single force left after opposing forces are combined: a 60 N push against 40 N of friction leaves a net 20 N.
The turning effect of a force, calculated as force times distance from the pivot, measured in newton-metres.
The fixed point a beam or lever turns around; every moment distance is measured from it.
Force spread over an area, calculated as force divided by area, measured in pascals.
The unit of pressure: one pascal is one newton spread over one square metre.

mechanismSteps: Friction opposes relative motion: a 60-newton push drives the block right, a 40-newton friction arrow grows at the contact against the slide, and the net 20 newtons to the right keeps the block sliding.

Moments: 60 newtons at 0.5 metres makes 30 newton-metres on the left; 30 newtons at 0.75 metres makes only 22.5 on the right, so the beam tips - then the right weight slides to 1.0 metre, its moment rises to 30, and the beam balances.
Pressure: a 200-newton crate on a 0.5-square-metre face gives 400 pascals; tipped onto a 0.05-square-metre edge the same force gives 4000 pascals - one tenth the area, ten times the pressure.
Check the thinking: the driving wheel pushes backward on the road at its contact patch, so friction pushes the car forward - friction opposes the relative slide, not the motion.
objectives: Find the net force when friction opposes a push, and explain why friction opposes relative slide rather than motion
Calculate a moment as force times distance from the pivot and use equal moments to balance a beam
Calculate pressure as force over area and predict how pressure changes when the area changes
subject: science
title: Forces: friction, moments and pressure

trap.explanation: The push feels the same, so the effect on the ground feels like it should be the same. Pressure is force over area: tiptoes spread the same force over a smaller area, so the pressure is higher. In class, keep the force fixed at 200 N and shrink only the area: 0.5 square metres gives 400 Pa, while 0.05 square metres gives 4000 Pa - the push never changed, only its spread.
trap.misconception: The same push gives the same pressure whether you stand flat or on tiptoes.

workedExample: A 200 N crate rests on its wide face of area 0.5 square metres. Pressure = force / area = 200 / 0.5 = 400 Pa. Check the units: newtons divided by square metres gives pascals, and tipping the crate onto a smaller face raises the pressure without changing the force.
